reviewed_before_change.input: One OpenCV-compatible BGR image; no explicit validation or defaults.
reviewed_before_change.result: The array returned by cv2.Canny, normally a single-channel uint8 edge image with the frame's height and width.
reviewed_before_change.mutation: Does not assign into or otherwise intentionally mutate frame; conversion, blur, and Canny create intermediate/result arrays.

module_imports: numpy (used by other functions in the module)
dependencies.video_demo_io: cv2.VideoCapture/imshow/waitKey/release/destroyAllWindows; moved under main() and mocked by the focused check.

test_fixture.input: 5x5 image where every BGR pixel is [0, 255, 0]
test_fixture.expected_canny_edges: 5x5 matrix of 0 (uniform input has no gradients)
test_fixture.method: Hand-calculate each intermediate state, inject those states at the cv2 boundary, then compare against function locals captured by sys.settrace.
test_fixture.scope_limit: cv2 and numpy are stubbed because they are not installed in the selected workspace environment; this verifies API wiring and mutation/return behavior, not OpenCV's native algorithms.

test_framework: Python standard-library unittest; the repository has no pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, tox.ini, or setup.cfg test configuration.
external_io: Video capture and display calls are mocked; no video file, camera, or GUI is opened.
